sources.citation: docs/victron-ve-direct-protocol-3.34.pdf — Victron Energy, VE.Direct Protocol, rev 3.34, 14 April 2025. Committed. Cited here for what it does not contain: the PID list, in full, for SmartShunt.
Retail: Quebec retailer sweep, checked: 2026-07-31 — SKUs SHU050130050, SHU065130050, SHU065150050, SHU065210050, SHU065220050.

gotchas: This is the finding, not a placeholder. VE.Direct Protocol 3.34's PID list — revised April 2025, so five years after the SmartShunt line was added — names exactly three SmartShunts: 500A/50mV 0xA389, 1000A/50mV 0xA38A, 2000A/50mV 0xA38B. It names no 300A and no IP65 variant. Grepping the full text of the committed PDF

Table I's column header is the class name `BMV71x SmartShunt`, so a class-level reading would sweep these in. The PID list is the model-level binding, and it does not. Those two readings disagree; both are recorded, and the catalogue follows the PID list because PID is the field a driver actually reads to decide what i
What would settle it: a bench capture of `PID` from a 300A or an IP65 SmartShunt, or a Victron document revision whose PID list names them. One capture closes this. It is an afternoon, not a week.
Five of the twelve SmartShunt SKUs in the Quebec retail set fall in this gap — the retailers stock ratings the protocol document has not caught up with. checked: 2026-07-31, 1 retailer each.
Do not guess a PID. Interpolating 0xA388 or 0xA38C from the surrounding ids would be exactly the fabrication the catalogue rules forbid, and it would cost whoever trusts it a day at the bench.
